title: OR Operator
description: Learn how to use the OR operator to combine two Boolean expressions in SQL Server, returning TRUE when either condition is true.

data.text: The SQL Server OR operator is a logical operator that allows you to combine two Boolean expressions. It returns TRUE when either of the conditions evaluates to TRUE.

data.title: OR Operator Syntax
data.content: Combine two Boolean expressions with OR.

data.text: In this syntax, the boolean_expression is any valid Boolean expression that evaluates to TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN.
The following table shows the results of the OR operator when combining TRUE, FALSE, and UNKNOWN:

data.title: Operator Precedence
data.text: When you use multiple logical operators in an expression, SQL Server always evaluates the OR operators after the AND operators. You can use parentheses () to change the order of evaluation.

data.title: Basic OR Example
data.content: Find products with list price less than 200 or greater than 6000.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    list_price < 200
    OR list_price > 6000
ORDER BY
    list_price;

data.title: Multiple OR Conditions
data.content: Find products with brand ID 1, 2, or 4.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    brand_id
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    brand_id = 1
    OR brand_id = 2
    OR brand_id = 4
ORDER BY
    brand_id DESC;

data.text: You can replace multiple OR operators with the IN operator, which is more concise:

data.title: Using IN Instead of Multiple ORs
data.content: IN is equivalent to multiple OR conditions.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    brand_id
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    brand_id IN (1, 2, 3)
ORDER BY
    brand_id DESC;

data.title: OR with AND
data.content: AND is evaluated first, so this means: (brand_id=2 AND list_price>500) OR brand_id=1.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    brand_id,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    brand_id = 1
    OR brand_id = 2
    AND list_price > 500
ORDER BY
    brand_id DESC,
    list_price;

data.text: In this example, SQL Server evaluated the AND operator first. Therefore, the query returned products whose brand ID is 2 and the list price is greater than 500, or those whose brand ID is 1.
To find products whose brand ID is 1 or 2 and list price is greater than 500, use parentheses:

data.title: OR with AND Using Parentheses
data.content: Parentheses change evaluation order so OR is evaluated first.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    brand_id,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    (brand_id = 1 OR brand_id = 2)
    AND list_price > 500
ORDER BY
    brand_id;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The OR operator combines two Boolean expressions and returns TRUE if either expression is TRUE.
OR has lower precedence than AND; use parentheses to control evaluation order.
Multiple OR conditions can be replaced with the more concise IN operator.
The OR truth table shows that OR returns TRUE if at least one operand is TRUE.
